intro: To schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac, open the Zoom Workplace desktop app, click Schedule on the Home tab, enter a topic, pick a date and time, add invitees, and click Save. If you would rather use a browser, sign in at zoom.us, click the Zoom Products icon, choose Meetings, then click Schedule a Meeting.
tldr: Open the Zoom Workplace desktop app and click Schedule on the Home tab.
Enter a topic, date, time and invitees, then click Save.
After Save, choose Send, Don't send, or Back to editing.
For a recurring meeting with no fixed time, use the web portal, Gmail, or Outlook.
On the Basic plan, Zoom's pricing page lists 40 minutes per meeting.

blocks.text: Most people who search this question want one of two things. Some want to book a meeting from the Zoom app already open on their Mac. Others work in a browser, or their company sends them to zoom.us for scheduling. This guide covers both. It starts with the desktop app, then covers the browser route and the edge cases that catch people out.
Which way to schedule a Zoom meeting on your Mac

Zoom offers more than one route, and the one you see depends on your setup. When calendar and contacts integration is on, Zoom's help article describes a Calendar tab route. When it is off, the route runs through the Meetings tab and its add icon. Zoom also lists a Scheduler tab for booking pages, and the web portal works from any browser. The table shows the routes side by side.

blocks.text: What you need before you schedule on a Mac

items: A Mac running macOS 10.15 or later
The Zoom Workplace desktop app, signed in to your Zoom account
Calendar and contacts integration turned on, if you want Zoom to send invitations
A processor and memory at or above the minimums: dual-core 2 GHz and 4 GB RAM

blocks.text: macOS 10.15 is the minimum for the current desktop app, according to Zoom's system requirements article. Zoom's 7.0.0 release notes say the app no longer supports macOS 10.13 or 10.14. If your Mac runs an older system, version 6.7.7 is the last release for anything below 10.15. To check your system, open the Apple menu, choose About This Mac, and read the macOS version in the window.

The processor and memory figures apply across platforms, not only Mac. Zoom lists them as minimums, so treat them as the floor, not a comfortable target. Open the app once before an important meeting. That way an update prompt does not catch you off guard in the middle of the day.
Fill in the New event window

The New event window is where the meeting gets its details. Start with the topic. Use a name your invitees will recognize in their own calendar, such as a project name and a month. Then set the date and start time. Check the time zone before you move on, because your invitees will read the time in their own zone. You can add invitees now or copy the link later.

Settings holds the meeting options. The Meeting ID field lets you choose Generate Automatically or your Personal Meeting ID. Passcode, Waiting room, Require authentication, Encryption, Zoom AI, and Meeting chat are all listed as supported on Mac. A Personal Meeting ID keeps the same ID each time, which can suit a recurring team stand-up. A generated ID suits a one-off call.
Meeting options to check before you save

Open Advanced before you save. It holds Allow participants to join anytime, with 5, 10, or 15 minutes, or Anytime. That setting controls how early people may join before the start time. A short window keeps people from drifting in early. Anytime suits an open office hours session where the room should stay available.

Some options exist only in the browser. Zoom's comparison table marks Registration, Whiteboard, focus mode, Breakout Room pre-assign, audio watermark, and sign language interpretation as web-only for scheduling. If you need one of them, schedule in the browser instead of the desktop app. The desktop steps will not show those fields.
Save the meeting and choose how to send it

Click Save, and Zoom offers three choices. Back to editing keeps the meeting open so you can change it. Don't send keeps the meeting without sending the invitation. Send sends the invitation now. If you still need to set a passcode or check the time zone, choose Back to editing first.

Automatic email invitations need calendar and contacts integration. Without it, copy the meeting details and send them yourself. Paste the join link, the date, the time, and the time zone into an email or chat. One line with the time zone saves a round of questions.
Schedule a Zoom meeting from the web portal instead

The browser route gives you the full set of options. Sign in at zoom.us, click the Zoom Products icon, and choose Meetings. Click Schedule a Meeting, complete the fields, select your options, and click Save. In the Zoom Web App, Home then Schedule redirects to this same web portal, so you land in the same place either way.

Choose the browser when the desktop window does not show what you need. Zoom's feature comparison says the desktop app on Mac can schedule one-time or recurring meetings, and can view, edit, start, or delete scheduled meetings. It describes the web portal as the place to schedule, view, and edit meetings. Both routes are real. Pick the one that shows the option you need.
Recurring meetings and the No fixed time problem

Recurring meetings are where the desktop app and the web portal disagree. Zoom's feature table says the desktop app can schedule recurring meetings. A separate Zoom help article says the No fixed time recurrence option was removed from the desktop client in April 2023. That article says the change affects desktop client version 5.14.5 or higher.

If you need a recurring meeting with no fixed end, Zoom recommends the web portal, Gmail, or Outlook. Set the recurrence in the browser, then check the meeting from the desktop app. Zoom's table says the app can view, edit, start, or delete scheduled meetings, so it stays useful after you create one.
What the free plan limit means for your schedule

Zoom's pricing page lists 40 minutes per meeting on the Basic plan. A scheduled call on Basic stops at 40 minutes. A longer planned session needs a paid plan, or a split into two meetings. The same page lists 30 hours for meetings on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans.

Prices change, so check the pricing page before you choose. When this guide was checked, Zoom listed Pro at $16.99 per user per month billed monthly, or $14.16 per user per month billed annually. Business listed $21.99 monthly or $18.33 annually. Enterprise had no listed price.
Mistakes people make when scheduling on a Mac
Watch for these four slips. Each one costs a few minutes, and each one is easy to avoid once you know it.

items: Clicking Don't send and then wondering why nobody got the invite.
Looking for the Calendar tab when integration is off. It will not appear, so use Meetings instead.
Expecting Registration or Whiteboard in the desktop app. Zoom's table marks those as web-only.
Missing a setting that will not change. Admins can lock some options at the account or group level, so ask your admin.

blocks.text: Next steps once the meeting is set

A scheduled meeting is only half the job. Check your camera permission before the call, share your screen when you need to, and record if your team wants a copy. These guides cover each one: [grant camera access](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom), [share your screen](/how-to/share-your-screen-in-zoom), [record a meeting](/how-to/record-a-meeting-in-zoom), and [change your virtual background](/how-to/change-your-virtual-background-in-zoom).

faq.question: Can I schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac without the desktop app?
faq.answer: Yes. Sign in at zoom.us, click the Zoom Products icon, choose Meetings, click Schedule a Meeting, complete the fields, and click Save. The browser route also gives you the web-only options.

faq.question: Where is the Schedule button in the Zoom Mac app?
faq.answer: On the Home tab in the Zoom Workplace desktop app. If Home is not visible, click More and choose Home. The Calendar and Meetings routes also work, depending on your integration setting.

faq.question: Does Zoom send the invitation automatically?
faq.answer: Not by itself. You choose Send after you save. Automatic email invitations need calendar and contacts integration turned on. Without it, copy the link and send it yourself.

faq.question: What is the minimum macOS version for the Zoom Workplace app?
faq.answer: macOS 10.15 or later, according to Zoom's system requirements article. Version 6.7.7 is the last release for systems below 10.15. Version 7.0.0 dropped support for macOS 10.13 and 10.14.

faq.question: Can I schedule a recurring meeting with no fixed time on Mac?
faq.answer: Not in the desktop app. Zoom removed the No fixed time option from the desktop client in April 2023. Use the web portal, Gmail, or Outlook for that kind of schedule.

faq.question: How long can a scheduled meeting run on the free plan?
faq.answer: Zoom's pricing page lists 40 minutes per meeting on the Basic plan. For longer sessions, check the pricing page for paid plans, which list 30 hours for meetings.

faq.question: What do Back to editing, Don't send, and Send do?
faq.answer: Back to editing keeps the meeting open so you can change it. Don't send saves the meeting without sending the invitation. Send sends the invitation now.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to schedule a meeting on Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom's official pages did not confirm one, so this guide leaves it out. Third-party lists disagree on the key combination. Check the app's settings for a keyboard shortcuts list before you rely on any shortcut.

task: Schedule a Zoom meeting on Mac
appliesTo: Zoom Workplace desktop app on macOS 10.15 or later, plus zoom.us in a browser
requirements: A Mac running macOS 10.15 or later
The Zoom Workplace desktop app, signed in to your Zoom account, or zoom.us in a browser

steps.name: Open Zoom Workplace and sign in
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace from Applications or Launchpad. Sign in with the Zoom account that will host the meeting. Zoom's help article bases its screens on version 6.7.0.
steps.tip: If your sidebar looks different, your version may be newer or older than 6.7.0. Keep going with the same labels.

steps.name: Click Home in the sidebar
steps.text: Click Home in the left sidebar. If you do not see it, click More, then choose Home. Zoom's article lists the sidebar as Chat, Calendar, Phone, Contacts, and Hub in version 6.7.0.
steps.tip: Home may sit under More on some layouts.

steps.name: Click Schedule
steps.text: Click Schedule. Zoom opens a window called New event. Everything you set for the meeting goes into this window before you save it.
steps.tip: If nothing opens, confirm you are on Home, not another tab, then try again.

steps.name: Enter a topic
steps.text: Click the Topic field and type a name. Pick a name your invitees will recognize in their own calendar, such as a project name and a month.

steps.name: Set the date and time
steps.text: Choose the date, then the start time. Check the time zone before you move on, because invitees read the time in their own zone.

steps.name: Add invitees (optional)
steps.text: Add email addresses in the invitees field if you want Zoom to send the invitation. Automatic email invitations need calendar and contacts integration turned on.
steps.tip: You can skip this step and copy the join link later.

steps.name: Open Settings for meeting options
steps.text: Click Settings to choose the Meeting ID, a passcode, the waiting room, encryption, and other options. Advanced holds the join-anytime window.
steps.tip: Some options may be locked by your admin.

steps.name: Click Save and choose how to send
steps.text: Click Save. Zoom asks you to pick Back to editing, Don't send, or Send. Choose Send to deliver the invitation now.
steps.tip: Choose Back to editing if you still need to change something.

troubleshooting.problem: Schedule is not on the Home tab
troubleshooting.fix: Click Home, or More then Home. If calendar and contacts integration is on, use the Calendar tab. If it is off, use the Meetings tab and its add icon. If the layout still differs, compare your app version with 6.7.0, the version Zoom's instructions are based on.

troubleshooting.problem: No No fixed time option for a recurring meeting
troubleshooting.fix: Zoom removed that option from the desktop client in April 2023, for version 5.14.5 and higher. Create the recurring meeting in the web portal, or in Gmail or Outlook, as Zoom recommends.
Automatic email invitations need calendar and contacts integration enabled. Turn it on, or copy the join link and send it yourself. Then check the invitee list before you choose Send.

troubleshooting.problem: The app will not install on an older Mac
troubleshooting.fix: The current app needs macOS 10.15 or later. The last release for older systems is 6.7.7. Check your macOS version under Apple menu, About This Mac first.
Your admin may have locked it at the account or group level. Ask your Zoom admin to lift that restriction, or check whether the option is one that only appears in the web portal.

lazur.result: Hold Option and Command and ask where Schedule is. Lazur circles and labels it on screen. Ask for a walkthrough and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
